changes.new: Door-to-door: three business days, and Saturday, Sunday and legal holidays do not count. Initial residential contract: until midnight at the end of the next business day.
changes.support: does not include a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday

changes.new: Over $2,000; written within 5 days if job grows (701.305); must show the contractor's name, address, phone and license number, the warranty offer acknowledgment where required, an explanation of the owner's rights, the customer and job address, the work, and price and payment terms, legible and in dark ink (OAR 812-012-0110)
changes.support: Everything "must be legible and in dark ink".

changes.new: CCB license; de minimis under $1,000 (not if advertised); the license number must be shown on written bids and building contracts
changes.support: All written bids, written inspection reports and building contracts subject to ORS chapter 701 shall show the contractor's license number.

changes.new: 701.560 to 701.605: owner sends notice by registered or certified mail; the contractor may ask to examine within 14 days and must respond within 90 days; the owner has 30 days to accept an offer
changes.support: not later than 90 days after the contractor, subcontractor or supplier receives a notice of defect or secondary notice

new.rule: Present the offer terms clearly and conspicuously next to the request for consent, get affirmative consent before charging, give a retainable acknowledgment with cancellation instructions, and offer an easy cancellation mechanism
new.scope_and_confidence: PRIMARY; applies to any automatic renewal or continuous service offer to a consumer in Oregon with no carve-out for household services

changes.support: with no carve-out for household services

unsure: OR-cancel: the next-business-day right has no prescribed wording and the statute does not require the contract to print it; I held it, though OAR 812-012-0110(1)(c) wants an owner's-rights explanation in the contract.
OR-ccb: I reused this notice for the Consumer Protection Notice because the first pass's OAR 812 entry is now identified as that form, and added the Notice of Procedure as its own notice.

OR-notice-of-procedure: loaded for print on every residential job over $2,000; the OAR ties delivery to contracts needing a written contract under ORS 701.305, which covers a residential structure or zero-lot-line dwelling, and the builder cannot check for the zero-lot-line case.
OR warranty offer (ORS 701.320): a written offer is required for new residential structures only, with no prescribed wording, so no notice was added.
OR day count: the next-business-day cancellation does not define business day in chapter 701, so I set saturday_counts false only on the strength of the door-to-door definition.

OR-door-to-door and OR-door-to-door-notice: printed on every sale at the customer's home; the statute says the seller may use the federal 16 CFR 429 notice instead of the Oregon notice (not the statement), and the builder cannot tell which the seller chose.

OR-door-to-door: the statement's last sentence points to the 'attached notice'; the statute says the seller must change that sentence if the two copies of the notice are not attached to the agreement, so the printed sentence is right only if they are attached.
